title: P46 (Chester Beatty II): 1 Corinthians 11:18-12:2 (fols. 52r-52v)
source: P46 (Chester Beatty Biblical Papyrus II, Chester Beatty Library, Dublin): photographs as published in the INTF New Testament Virtual Manuscript Room; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P46; English from the King James Version
description: 1 Corinthians 11:18-12:2 in P46, the papyrus codex of Paul's letters copied around 200: fols. 52r-52v, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P46 is a papyrus codex of the letters of Paul copied in Egypt around 200, the oldest surviving collection of Paul's letters. 86 of its 104 leaves survive: 56 in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (Biblical Papyrus II, published by Frederic Kenyon in 1934-1937) and 30 in the University of Michigan Library, Ann Arbor (P.Mich. inv. 6238, published by Henry Sanders in 1935). The letters run in the order Romans, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, Philippians, Colossians and 1 Thessalonians; the first seven leaves (Romans 1:1-5:17) and the end of the book are lost. Hebrews standing after Romans, and the doxology of Romans (16:25-27) standing after 15:33, are among its best-known features.

Each section below is one page side: the holding library's photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse that has text on the page. The lower lines of many leaves are lost; the transcribers' restorations are in square brackets.

This entry covers fols. 52r-52v (1 Corinthians 11:18-12:2).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>11:18</sup>For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it. <sup>19</sup>For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you. <sup>20</sup>When ye come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lord’s supper. <sup>21</sup>For in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken. <sup>22</sup>What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not. <sup>23</sup>For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: <sup>24</sup>And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me. <sup>25</sup>After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.

translation.text: <sup>11:26</sup>For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come. <sup>27</sup>Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. <sup>28</sup>But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup. <sup>29</sup>For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. <sup>30</sup>For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. <sup>31</sup>For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged. <sup>32</sup>But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. <sup>33</sup>Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, tarry one for another. <sup>34</sup>And if any man hunger, let him eat at home; that ye come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come. <sup>12:1</sup>Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. <sup>2</sup>Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.
